results.title: Sir Sam Jonah says true legacy lies in how others remember you
results.content: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has urged people to reflect on how their actions affect others, saying a person's legacy is ultimately determined by the memories and experiences of those whose lives they have touched. Delivering the keynote address at the 2026 TrueLife Experience at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra, he described legacy as something people speak about when the person concerned is no longer present to shape the narrative. “It is a funeral word. It is what they say in the tributes, after the second hymn, when you are in no position to correct the facts. So when I was asked to speak on legacy, I did what any sensible man of my vintage would do. I checked my pulse,” he said, drawing laughter from the audience. Sir Sam Jonah said he approaches the concept of legacy with caution, arguing that people cannot determine how they will ultimately be remembered.

results.title: Losing my son made me value time with loved ones more – Sir Sam Jonah
results.content: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has spoken about the loss of his son, Richard, saying the experience changed his perspective on life and made him more conscious of the importance of spending time with loved ones. Delivering the keynote address at the 2026 TrueLife Experience at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra, he reflected on the limits of authority and influence in the face of personal loss. “There are experiences in which the authority you exercise elsewhere offers you no protection. You cannot negotiate your way out of grief. You cannot summon the right people into a room and ask them to resolve it. You are a father who has lost his son,” he said. Sir Sam Jonah said he did not want to turn his son's life or death into a lesson for his audience.

results.title: Nobody succeeds alone – Sir Sam Jonah reflects on journey to business leadership
results.content: Business leader and Chancellor of the University of Cape Coast, Sir Sam Jonah, has challenged the notion of the self-made individual, saying his rise to the top of the mining industry was made possible by the support, guidance and opportunities provided by others. Delivering the keynote address at the 2026 TrueLife Experience at the Kempinski Hotel in Accra, he reflected on his journey from the mining town of Obuasi to becoming chief executive of Ashanti Goldfields at the age of 36. “I did not get there alone, and I want to say so plainly, because self-made is one of the great lies of public life. Nobody is self-made,” he said. “There were men who taught me, men who covered for my mistakes, and men who took a risk on me when the safer bet was obvious,” he added.
